Project Management Tools Comparison

Six tools compared across ten criteria, with a recommendation

1. Overview

This document compares six widely used project-management tools: Asana, monday.com, Jira Software, ClickUp, Trello and Wrike. Each is assessed against ten criteria grouped into five categories: cost, users, functionality, connectivity and insight, and governance.

Pricing is approximate US list pricing per user per month on annual billing, based on published plans as known at the time of writing. Vendors change plans frequently, so confirm current prices on each vendor's website before purchasing. Feature availability is summarised at tier level and may differ by plan.

3. Criteria Notes

  • Price: Paid per-user prices on annual billing. Minimum seat counts (monday.com) and add-ons can raise the real cost.
  • Free tier: Useful for pilots. Seat caps and feature limits usually make free tiers unsuitable beyond evaluation.
  • Best-fit team size: A general guide to where each tool's structure and cost work best, not a hard limit.
  • Ease of learning: Judged by how quickly a new user can create and update tasks without training.
  • Views and work modes: Lists, boards, timelines, Gantt charts and workload views. Software teams often need sprints and backlogs.
  • Automation: No-code rules that move tasks, set fields and notify people. Quotas on actions vary by tier.
  • Collaboration and docs: Built-in documents, forms, proofing and discussion features that reduce tool switching.
  • Integrations: Breadth and depth of native connections. Developer-centric integrations are strongest in Jira.
  • Reporting and analytics: Dashboards, burndown or velocity charts, and portfolio views. Advanced reporting usually sits behind higher tiers.
  • Security and admin controls: SSO, audit logs, granular permissions and data residency. These typically require enterprise plans.

4. Recommendation

The right tool depends on the team's work type and how much governance it needs. The guidance below is a starting point.

Best overall for general business teams: Asana or monday.com

Both offer a polished, easy-to-learn experience across marketing, operations and project delivery. Asana suits teams that want clean workflows and strong portfolio views. monday.com suits teams that want highly customisable boards and a wide range of visual options.

Best for software and engineering teams: Jira Software

Its agile boards, sprint reporting and developer toolchain integrations are hard to match. Expect a steeper learning curve for non-technical stakeholders, and consider Confluence for documentation.

Best value for a single tool covering many functions: ClickUp

A generous free tier and a wide feature set make it attractive for cost-conscious teams. The breadth can overwhelm new users, so plan for a configuration and onboarding effort.

Best for simple workflows and small teams: Trello

The lowest cost and fastest onboarding of the six. It is a good fit for kanban-style work, but reporting and advanced planning are limited. Teams often outgrow it.

Best for mid-size to enterprise creative and professional services: Wrike

Strong request management, proofing and real-time dashboards make it a good fit for marketing and agency workflows. It has a learning curve and higher per-seat cost at the business tier.

Suggested decision approach

  1. Identify the primary work type: general projects, software delivery, creative work or simple task tracking.
  2. Shortlist two tools and run a 30-day pilot with real projects, using each tool's free or trial tier.
  3. Check the must-have integrations and security requirements (SSO, audit logs) before committing.
  4. Confirm current pricing and seat minimums with each vendor, then compare total annual cost including add-ons.
